```{r}
# Loading packages
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(kableExtra)
library(leaflet)

# Loading data
zum_data <- read_csv("SampleZumExport.csv")
neighborhood_boundaries <- st_read("boston_neighborhood_boundaries.geojson.json", quiet = TRUE)
```

## Overview

I chose to complete the Corner Stops technical exercise. This exercise combines Zum export data on bus routes with spatial data that defines Boston neighborhood boundaries. There are two deliverables:

1.  A summary table of the largest corner stops by neighborhood

2.  A map of the 50 largest corner stops

In addition to these deliverables, I will provide justification for some of the decisions and assumptions that I made.

## Assumptions and Decisions

```{r}
# Summarizing bus stops by AM/PM bell times, excluding actual school buildings
stop_summary <- zum_data %>%
  # Reshaping data to long format to more easily identify AM/PM via bell times
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      `Bell Time - Mo`:`Bell Time - Fr`,
      `Event Time - Mo`:`Event Time - Fr`
    ),
    names_to = c(".value", "day"),
    names_pattern = "(Bell Time|Event Time) - (Mo|Tu|We|Th|Fr)"
  ) %>%
  # Dropping rows with missing event times
  filter(!is.na(`Event Time`)) %>%
  # Group by unique stop locations
  group_by(
    `Event Address`, `Event lat`, `Event lng`, `Is Campus`
  ) %>%
  #Aggregate student and school counts by AM/PM bell times
  summarize(
    total_students = n_distinct(`Student ID`),
    morning_students = n_distinct(`Student ID`[hour(`Bell Time`) < 12]),
    afternoon_students = n_distinct(`Student ID`[hour(`Bell Time`) >= 12]),
    total_schools = n_distinct(`School Name`),
    morning_schools = n_distinct(`School Name`[hour(`Bell Time`) < 12]),
    afternoon_schools = n_distinct(`School Name`[hour(`Bell Time`) >= 12]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Not interested in schools as stops themselves
  filter(`Is Campus` == FALSE)

# Finding stops with multiple lat/lng
# zum_data %>% select(`Event Address`, `Event lat`, `Event lng`) %>% unique() %>% group_by(`Event Address`) %>% summarize(n = n()) %>% filter(n>1)

```

- Size of stop is measured by the number of distinct students serviced by the stop

- Campus stops were excluded, as the analysis is focused on corner stops

- Corner stops were grouped by latitude and longitude coordinates in addition to address. There were three instances where the same stop had multiple coordinates, and these were treated as separate stops

- I defined morning/afternoon (AM/PM) using bell times (before noon vs noon or later)

- Records with missing Event Times were excluded because they represent days where the stop was not serviced

## Top Stop By Neighborhood

The table below shows the largest stop in each neighborhood in Boston. This includes the number of unique students served, the percentage of total neighborhood stop assignments that the stop represents, the number of students served in the morning and afternoon, and the number of unique schools serviced by the stop.

```{r}
# Using long/lat coordinates to create sf object
stops_sf <- stop_summary %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("Event lng", "Event lat"), crs = 4326)

# Join didn't work initially, so fixing
neighborhood_boundaries_fixed <- st_make_valid(neighborhood_boundaries)

# Spatial join between stops_sf and neighborhood boundaries
stops_with_neighborhoods <- st_join(stops_sf, neighborhood_boundaries_fixed, join = st_intersects)

# Creating summary table with top stop per neighborhood
top_neighborhood_stops <- stops_with_neighborhoods %>%
  # Getting rid of geometry column
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  # Also calculating percentage of total neighborhood assignments per stop
  mutate(neighborhood_total_students = sum(total_students)) %>%
  slice_max(total_students, n = 1) %>%
  mutate(pct_neighborhood_students = paste0(round(total_students/neighborhood_total_students, 2)*100, "%")) %>%
  select(neighborhood = `name`, `Event Address`, `total_students`, 
         `pct_neighborhood_students`,  
         `morning_students`, `afternoon_students`, 
         `total_schools`, `morning_schools`, `afternoon_schools`) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_students))

top_neighborhood_stops %>%
  kbl(col.names = c("Neighborhood", "Stop Address", "Students", "Neighborhood Percent", "Students (AM)", "Students (PM)", "Schools Serviced", "Schools (AM)", "Schools (PM)"),
      caption = "Largest Corner Stop by Boston Neighborhood",
      align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
  


```

## Mapping Top 50 Stops

Below is a map of the 50 largest stops by unique students. The size of each circle scales with the size of the stop, and more information is available by hovering each stop.

```{r}
# Selecting the top 50 stops
top_50_stops <- stops_with_neighborhoods %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  # Calculating percent of neighborhood students, like above
  mutate(neighborhood_total_students = sum(total_students),
         pct_neighborhood_students = 
           round(total_students/neighborhood_total_students, 2) * 100) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(total_students)) %>%
  # Only keeping the 50 largest stops
  head(50) %>% 
  # Creating the caption here for the map
  mutate(
    caption = paste0(
      "<b>Stop:</b> ",`Event Address`, "<br>",
      "<b>Students (AM/PM): </b>", `total_students`, " ", "(", 
      morning_students, "/", afternoon_students, ")",  "<br>",
      "<b>Percent of Neighborhood:</b> ", pct_neighborhood_students, "%"
    )
  )


# Create leaflet map
leaflet(top_50_stops) %>%
  # Using standard OpenStreetMap tiles
  addTiles(
    # Setting the minimum zoom so you can't zoom all the way out
    options = tileOptions(minZoom = 11)
  ) %>%
  # Adding neighborhood boundaries first
  addPolygons(data = neighborhood_boundaries_fixed,
              color = "#1d3557",
              fillColor = "#286eb7",
              fillOpacity = 0.3,
              label = ~name) %>%
  # Adding markers for each stop
  addCircleMarkers(
    color = "#A6192E",
    stroke = FALSE,
    fillOpacity = 0.8,
    # Size of circle is a function of students serviced
    radius = ~sqrt(total_students)*0.8,
    label = ~lapply(caption, htmltools::HTML)
  ) %>%
  # Adding a title
  addControl("<h3 style='margin: 0;'>Top BPS Bus Stops</h3>", position = "topright")
    



```
